item.title: Signs that Your Backup Generator Needs Repairs
item.dc:creator: mediagistic
item.content:encoded:
Power outages can strike at any time in Larchmont, NY, so you can't afford to take chances with your backup generator. If you've experienced any of the following issues, it's time to have your generator checked by a qualified service technician.

Trouble Starting or Staying Running

When properly installed, your standby generator should fire up within seconds of an outage and continue operating smoothly until power is restored. If it has trouble starting up, there may be a problem with the battery, spark plug, ignition coil, or fuel system. After starting up, check to see if the generator runs roughly or makes unusual noises. This may suggest a fuel issue, faulty sensor, low oil level, or internal engine malfunction. Regardless of the cause, scheduling backup generator repairs right away will ensure the situation doesn't get worse. `

Unsteady or Insufficient Power Flow

A backup generator is meant to supply a steady, uninterrupted flow of power into your home. You should never encounter dimming lights, underpowered appliances, tripped circuit breakers, or any other signs of fluctuating output. Inconsistent power flow may occur for many reasons, including damaged internal components, bad electrical connections, or a faulty phase selector switch. Not only are these issues frustrating to deal with, but they can potentially damage sensitive electronics. If your generator is struggling to reliably meet your power needs, a professional repair call is in order.

Visibly Damaged or Worn-Out Equipment

Standby generators are built to be rugged and reliable, but that doesn't mean they're indestructible. That's why having your equipment serviced at least once a year is essential. It's a good idea to periodically conduct your own basic visual inspections between service visits. In particular, look for loose hoses or electrical connections, frayed wires, fluid leaks, and damaged or corroded parts. Additionally, start your generator up and ensure it isn't producing any strange noises or odors during operation. When it comes to your generator, dealing with problems proactively can end up saving you a lot of trouble. For speedy 24-hour backup generator repairs in Larchmont and surrounding communities, contact the qualified service technicians at G.C. Reliable Service.

Strange Smells

If your furnace is having issues with a gas leak or it is dealing with intrusive dust, then it may start emitting strong odors. While the unit may have a strong scent when you first use it, these smells are more pervasive and abnormal.

Your pilot light should be blue as it operates as an ignition source. Keep an eye on it and make note of any discoloration. If your furnace is having problems with heat output, then this could be a sign that there is something wrong with your thermostat or that the ductwork is faulty. Your furnace should do its job; when it fails to do that, it is time to call in HVAC experts.

Continuous Racket

Furnaces will make noise — that's a given. But when they start making persistent attention-grabbing squeals and whistles, then it may be time for a furnace repair. Persistent squeals and whistles are most associated with belt or fan problems. Additionally, bangs and groans can often be tied to broken and loose internal pieces.

Blocking direct sunlight from your interior spaces helps to keep your home cooler, making your air conditioner's job easier. Use window blinds and keep the curtains closed to help prevent your home from becoming needlessly hot. Pay special attention to the windows located on the southern part of your home.

2. Utilize Ceiling Fans

Using ceiling fans while your AC is running helps circulate the cool air. This circulation can make the room feel cooler, allowing you to raise the temperature settings on the thermostat by a few degrees. Keeping your thermostat higher will consume less energy, saving you money.

3. Keep Exterior Doors Shut

To ensure your air conditioner runs efficiently, keeping the doors and windows of your home shut is essential. Cool air escapes, and hot air enters when windows or external doors are open. Consider adding weather stripping to your doors and windows to seal potential air leaks.

4. Regular AC System Maintenance

Air conditioning systems require regular maintenance to ensure they're energy-efficient when cooling your home. Depending on the AC system type, you must replace or clean your air filters every few months. Additionally, schedule regular professional maintenance so a technician can perform routine maintenance that keeps your system running optimally. By implementing these tips, you can enjoy a cool and comfortable home while ensuring your energy bills remain reasonable. item.title: Ductless Mini-Splits : Efficient and Versatile HVAC
item.dc:creator: mediagistic
item.content:encoded:
Offering an appealing alternative to central-air HVAC systems, ductless mini-splits keep your indoor environment comfortable without using ductwork in White Plains, NY. The absence of ducts makes these innovative heat pumps adaptable to virtually any application. Taking ductwork out of the equation also saves energy, making mini-splits some of the most efficient HVAC systems available today.

How Ductless Mini-Splits Work

Like any other heat pump system, ductless mini-splits work by extracting heat from the air and moving it elsewhere. They use refrigerant to pull warm air out of your home or business during the summer and bring it indoors during the winter. It's the way they do it that differentiates mini-splits from other heat pump systems. Instead of using a network of air ducts to circulate the conditioned air, ductless mini-splits use independently operating air handlers linked to a single outdoor unit. Each air handling unit has its own thermostat, so you can set different temperatures in different living spaces. Autonomous operation also means there's no need to condition rooms that aren't occupied, saving you money on heating and cooling.

Versatile Installation

Ductless mini-splits connect to the outdoor unit using sleek conduits that house the power cable, refrigerant lines and condensate drain. A three-inch hole drilled behind each handler is the only alteration needed to accommodate the installation. This non-intrusive design makes mini-splits ideal for almost any situation, from structures that can't accommodate ductwork systems to remodeled spaces such as basements, attics, and enclosed porches.

Superior Energy Efficiency

In the average ducted HVAC system, leaks, loose connections, and inadequate insulation can account for more than 30% of the energy used. Heating or cooling rooms you aren't using also wastes and energy and money. Superior energy efficiency makes ductless mini-splits a sound investment in indoor comfort. The secret to getting the most from your ductless system lies in partnering with an HVAC company that knows mini-splits inside and out. At G.C. Normal Heat Pump Sounds

Your heat pump will most likely make a humming or whirring sound when operating as it should. The AC contactors and coils may also make a slight buzzing sound as electricity runs through them. A light clicking often indicates when the unit cycles on and off. It's normal for a heat pump to make a small amount of noise when running. However, if you notice loud or unusual sounds coming from your heat pump, it's time to call an HVAC professional.

When It's Time to Call a Professional

If the specific sound or the level of noise becomes concerning, it may be time to seek professional assistance. A hissing sound coming from your heat pump often indicates a refrigerant leak. A loose, displaced or broken component inside the unit may cause a banging or rattling sound. A problem with your heat pump's fan may cause thumping or knocking. The fan may be damaged, unbalanced or otherwise malfunctioning. If the damage is very severe, the fan may require replacement.

Why Invest in Seasonal Maintenance?

Oftentimes, an HVAC professional can detect the early signs of a problem with your heat pump before the unusual noises begin. Therefore, it is critical that you have your HVAC inspected at least annually. Homeowners trust our team with their heat pump maintenance and repairs needs. It's an unfortunate fact that no heat pumps will last forever. Deciding between a heat pump repair and replacement can be difficult sometimes, but getting the decision right can save you a considerable amount of money and frustration. Read on to learn about some of the criteria for deciding what to do about your Pelham, NY, heat pump.

The Age of Your Heat Pump

On average, heat pumps last roughly 12-15 years, but regular maintenance and timely repairs could extend your heat pump's lifespan to 20 years or a little more. It's often more cost-effective in the long run to replace older systems than to continue paying for frequent repairs and increased energy bills.

Sharply Rising Energy Bills

Ominous Noises

While it's normal for heat pumps to make a small amount of noise, any loud or distressing sounds likely indicate a problem. Whenever you hear strange or excessively loud noises coming from your HVAC equipment, it's wise to schedule a service call with an expert. It's important to note that ominous noises and rising utility costs don't necessarily mean that it's time to replace your system. A qualified professional can address any concerns you might have and help you determine whether repairing or replacing your equipment would be in your best interest.

The Cost of Repairs

As a general rule, if your heat pump's repair will cost 50% or more of the cost of a new heat pump, then it makes sense to replace it. Natural gas is odorless in its raw state. Gas companies add a sulfur smell to it for safety. If you smell something like sulfur or rotten eggs, then you have a gas leak. In this case, you need to act quickly and safely. Open your home's windows after shutting off the furnace, and then ask an HVAC technician to investigate and make any necessary repairs.

3. Smoke

As the saying goes, "Where there's smoke, there's fire." Because the presence of smoke could mean that your furnace is on fire, this situation also requires swift action. Turn off your furnace, exit your home, and seek professional help immediately .

4. Dirty Socks

A smell like dirty socks indicates the presence of biological growth somewhere in either the furnace itself or in the ducts. Generally, this occurs because of standing water inside the system. item.title: Why Is My Ductless Mini-Split So Loud in New Rochelle, NY?
item.dc:creator: mediagistic
item.content:encoded:
A ductless mini-split system normally doesn't make any noises much louder than a whisper while functioning. A loud system is probably not functioning correctly and will likely use extra energy without heating or cooling your New Rochelle, NY home properly. Consider the following noises your ductless mini-split system can make and what they mean.

Grinding

Certain parts and bearings may grind together when they wear down with use or run out of oil. They may break or crack at some point, causing pinholes or other problems if you don't attend to them immediately.

Clicking

A faulty thermostat can cause your system to short cycle, which uses much more energy than necessary. This can add undue stress on the system and could cause permanent damage if the problem continues for too long. This type of issue typically manifests with additional clicking.

Buzzing

An outdoor compressor with electrical problems can emit loud buzzing noises and will use extra energy. Loud buzzing typically accompanies broken fan blades that may come loose and hit other parts, so promptly schedule repairs in these cases.

Bubbling or Hissing

Refrigerant lines should always have a tight seal and function without any leaks, but air bubbles may develop if there's a problem. You may also hear hissing noises, indicating that refrigerant is escaping. A qualified technician can help you by repairing your mini-split system. Avoid the headache of living with a noisy mini-split system and prevent further damage by getting expert help. item.title: 3 Tips for Improving Your Home's Airflow in Bronxville, NY
item.dc:creator: mediagistic
item.content:encoded:
Maintaining proper airflow throughout your Bronxville, NY, home helps keep you comfortable and improves indoor air quality. Here are some tips that can help you ensure maximum airflow in your home.

1. Replace Your HVAC Air Filter Regularly

Your HVAC plays a major role in keeping air circulating through your home. As it runs, it also passes your home's air through an air filter that traps dust, dirt and contaminants. If that filter gets too dirty, your home's airflow suffers. To prevent air filter problems, you should make a point of replacing yours approximately every three months. Doing so is an essential part of regular HVAC maintenance. It will help your HVAC provide adequate airflow and extend its lifespan.

2. Keep Your Air Vents Open

Another effective way to maintain proper airflow throughout your home is to open all your HVAC vents. You may believe that closing your vents is the appropriate way to adjust the temperature in individual rooms. However, doing so obstructs your HVAC system's ability to circulate air. In addition to keeping your vents open, make sure that they’re not blocked by furniture or other large items. Typically, you should keep around one foot of space between your vents and the objects closest to them.

3. Periodically Open Windows

Finally, you might want to make a habit of opening your home's windows when weather permits. Most modern homes are well-sealed to maximize energy efficiency, which means you won't get much natural ventilation unless you open windows. Neglecting to do so occasionally can contribute to stale and polluted air in your home. If the HVAC in your Bronxville, NY, home isn't providing sufficient airflow, it may need repair. item.title: 5 Tips for Boosting Airflow in Your Home in Harrison, NY
item.dc:creator: mediagistic
item.content:encoded:
Stagnant air can make your home feel stuffy and unpleasant. It can also trap odors inside your home. Use these five tips to improve airflow in your home in Harrison, NY.

1. Remove Obstacles

Obstacles like draperies, furniture, and boxes in front of the vents can compromise your home's airflow. To ensure your HVAC system can function efficiently, move anything that could block the vents. Likewise, keep the area around the indoor and outdoor units clean to ensure they function normally.

2. Schedule Seasonal Tune-ups

Regular maintenance can help your HVAC system work normally and improve airflow. This service involve removing debris cleaning off the outdoor unit and changing your HVAC system's air filter. You should hire an HVAC technician to maintain your system at least twice a year.

3. Address Unusual Noises

Unusual noises can tip you off that your AC needs repairs to improve airflow. For example, whistling noises can indicate a problem like cracks or holes in the ductwork. They can also occur when there are clogs in your vents.

4. Use Ceiling Fans

Ceiling fans can improve the flow of air inside your house. During the summer, run your ceiling fan in a counterclockwise direction to push air downward. During the winter, run it clockwise to pull up cool air and circulate warm air near the ceiling back into the room.

5. Invest in a Whole-Home Ventilator

Having a professional install a whole-home ventilator can significantly improve your home’s airflow throughout the year. This systems include both intake and exhaust vents bring in fresh air from outdoors while also expelling older air along with airborne contaminants that can otherwise build up to unhealthy levels. item.title: 4 Signs You Need a New Pool Heater in Harrison, NY
item.dc:creator: mediagistic
item.content:encoded:
Late spring in Harrison, NY is the time to prepare your pool and heater for the summer months ahead. This is the perfect time to service and turn on your heater to make sure it is working properly. Here are four signs that you need a new pool heater.

1. Age of the Heater

Pool heaters have a limited lifespan and will eventually need replacement. Gas heaters last for seven to 12 years, whereas electric heaters have a lifespan of 10 to 20 years. Solar pool heaters typically last the longest, with an average lifespan of 15 to 20 years. If your heater is out of warranty or has exceeded its useful lifespan, it's time to consider replacing it. Your pool heater installation and service provider can assess the age and condition of the heater and recommend a replacement, if necessary.

2. Water Temperature Isn’t Consistent

Sometimes the pool water takes too long to warm up or one area feels warmer than another area. Inconsistent water temperature and heating times are often due to a malfunctioning thermostat or non-working heating elements. A professional inspection will determine what the issue is and if replacement is in order.

3. Troublesome Noises

Unusual noises coming from your pool's heater are cause for concern. If you hear banging, grinding or whining coming from the unit, this is a sign that the heater has broken internal parts, such as a fan, burner or compressor, depending on the type of heater.

4. Reduced Water Flow

Water that isn’t circulating efficiently through the heater indicates a blockage or a pump issue. Reduced water flow will eventually cause the heater to completely shut down or to overheat. Immediate repairs are necessary before we recommend complete pool heater replacement. Heater replacement for your Harrison, NY pool is inevitable over time. If you suspect that you have a broken pool heater or if your pool is simply too old, contact GC Reliable Service for an inspection and installation of a new pool heater. Image provided by iStock
